title: What Is Tourette's Syndrome Really Like? A Clinical Psychologist Explains

sentences.en: What if your professional expertise could earn you money even when you're not working?
sentences.zh: 如果你的专业知识即使在你没工作时也能为你赚钱，那会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and since 2019 I've been building additional income streams
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在建立额外的收入来源，

sentences.en: through books, online courses and memberships, and it's made such a difference to my business and my life.
sentences.zh: 通过书籍、在线课程和会员制，这给我的事业和生活带来了巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Tonight at 7pm, Sophie Foote is hosting a free Make Money Online Masterclass, exploring how you can turn your existing skills and knowledge into additional income streaMs.
sentences.zh: 今晚7点，苏菲·富特将举办一场免费的“在线赚钱大师班”，探讨如何将你现有的技能和知识转化为额外的收入来源。

sentences.en: And I'd love more psychologists and mental health professionals to join us.
sentences.zh: 我非常希望更多的心理学家和心理健康专业人士能加入我们。

sentences.en: I'll be there too, supporting a lovely community of fellow psychologists, exploring what's possible beyond one-to-one work.
sentences.zh: 我也会在那里，支持一个可爱的心理学家同行社区，探索一对一工作之外的可能性。

sentences.en: Replays are available if you can't join live.
sentences.zh: 如果你无法参加直播，可以观看回放。

sentences.en: Click the link with this pre-roll or reach out to me on socials to grab your free place, because you can serve others and deserve financial freedom too.
sentences.zh: 点击此预告片旁边的链接，或在社交媒体上联系我以获取免费名额，因为你既可以服务他人，也理应获得财务自由。

sentences.en: Most people think Tourette's means swearing.
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为妥瑞症意味着说脏话。

sentences.en: In reality, about 95% of people with Tourette's don't swear at all.
sentences.zh: 实际上，约95%的妥瑞症患者根本不会说脏话。

sentences.en: So why has one of the most misunderstood neurodevelopmental conditions become defined by a symptom that most people never experience?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么这种最被误解的神经发育障碍之一，会被大多数人从未经历过的症状所定义呢？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, and today I'm joined by fellow clinical psychologist, Dr. Jason Codner, as we attempt to separate myth from reality.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，今天我的嘉宾是临床心理学家同行杰森·科德纳博士，我们将尝试拨开迷雾，还原真相。

sentences.en: We're exploring the impact that Tourette's can have on everyday life, as well as exploring the treatments and support that can help.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨妥瑞症对日常生活的影响，以及可以提供帮助的治疗和支持方式。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to Psychology Actually.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到《心理学其实》。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: I'm joined here today by a fellow qualified clinical psych.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾也是一位合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Hi, Jason.
sentences.zh: 嗨，杰森。

sentences.en: Please do introduce yourself.
sentences.zh: 请做一下自我介绍。

sentences.en: Hi, my name's Dr. Jason Codner, and I'm the principal clinical psychologist at the Northamptonshire
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫杰森·科德纳博士，是北安普敦郡

sentences.en: Healthcare NHS Trust, and I currently work in the adult ADHD autism and Tourette service.
sentences.zh: 医疗国民保健署（NHS）信托基金的首席临床心理学家，目前在成人多动症、自闭症和妥瑞症服务部门工作。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Beautiful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And yeah, it was having done an episode with one of your colleagues previously that made me have a little look on your trust website, and I realised that your service existed.
sentences.zh: 是的，之前我和你的一位同事做了一期节目，这让我去看了看你们信托基金的网站，我才意识到你们的服务存在。

sentences.en: And I thought, that's not something we've ever covered on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我想，这还没在我们播客里讲过。

sentences.en: So could you tell us a little bit about what Tourette's is?
sentences.zh: 那么你能告诉我们妥瑞症到底是什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so our trust and our team has been in existence for, gosh, for nearly 20 years now,
sentences.zh: 好的，我们的信托基金和团队已经存在，天哪，快20年了，

sentences.en: 20 plus years, and we've always done assessments for Tourette's in that time.
sentences.zh: 20多年了，在这期间我们一直都在进行妥瑞症的评估。

sentences.en: As a condition, Tourette's is a neurodevelopmental condition.
sentences.zh: 妥瑞症是一种神经发育障碍。

sentences.en: So what that means is it usually starts in childhood and often continues on into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它通常始于童年，并往往持续到成年。

sentences.en: And it's characterised often by both motor and physical tics.
sentences.zh: 它通常表现为运动抽动和发声抽动。

sentences.en: They have to occur both together, so it can't just be vocal tics and it can't just be motor tics.
sentences.zh: 它们必须同时出现，所以不能只有发声抽动，也不能只有运动抽动。

sentences.en: It's got to be both sets of presentation together, really.
sentences.zh: 确实必须是这两类表现同时存在。

sentences.en: And then starting in childhood, not better explained by something else.
sentences.zh: 而且始于童年，且不能用其他原因更好地解释。

sentences.en: And then once we do the assessment bit, if all the conditions are met, then we would usually give a diagnosis of Tourette's family.
sentences.zh: 评估完成后，如果所有条件都满足，我们通常会给出妥瑞症的诊断。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So I've already learned something, because I'm sure when I last learned about it, I was working with people with tick disorder, which I understand is a bit different.
sentences.zh: 所以我已经学到了一些东西，因为我记得上次了解它时，我是在和患有抽动障碍的人一起工作，我理解那是有所不同的。

sentences.en: We were kind of grouping as a neurological disorder, but it's now thought of as neurodevelopmental, Jason.
sentences.zh: 我们当时把它归类为神经系统疾病，但现在它被认为是神经发育障碍，杰森。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose if you want to get really bored.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你想听点枯燥的内容的话。

sentences.en: So in the DSM-5, so the Diagnostical Statistical Manual Version 5, which is the American sort of manual for diagnosing mental health and neurodevelopmental disorders,
sentences.zh: 在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》第5版（DSM-5）中，这是美国用于诊断心理健康和神经发育障碍的手册，

sentences.en: it falls currently in their neurodevelopmental category.
sentences.zh: 它目前被归入神经发育障碍类别。

sentences.en: But before 2013, there wasn't a category for neurodevelopmental disorders.
sentences.zh: 但在2013年之前，并没有“神经发育障碍”这个类别。

sentences.en: It was, I think it was disease of childhood or starting in the developmental period.
sentences.zh: 我想当时它被归为儿童疾病或发育期开始的疾病。

sentences.en: So the neurodevelopmental bit comes from the DSM-5, and I think it's just their umbrella term for all the conditions that started in childhood
sentences.zh: 所以“神经发育”这个词来自DSM-5，我认为这只是他们对所有始于童年

sentences.en: and that might continue on into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 并可能持续到成年的疾病的统称。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: Thank you for that clarification.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的澄清。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think Tourette's gets misunderstood because I don't think people realise how much of an impact it can have on your life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为妥瑞症被误解了，因为我觉得人们没有意识到它会对生活产生多大的影响。

sentences.en: I know there's been lots of stuff in the media since the Netflix film called I Swear, which is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我知道自从那部名为《我发誓》（I Swear）的Netflix纪录片上映后，媒体上有很多相关报道，那部片子很棒。

sentences.en: I've watched it.
sentences.zh: 我看过。

sentences.en: Really, really interesting.
sentences.zh: 真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I also follow a really great creator called Luke Manton on LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 而且我在领英上关注了一位非常棒的创作者，叫卢克·曼顿。

sentences.en: If people don't already follow him, I would recommend that because he has Tourette's himself.
sentences.zh: 如果大家还没关注他，我推荐关注，因为他本人就患有妥瑞症。

sentences.en: So I feel like I've learned a bit more through both of those kind of case studies, if you will.
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉通过这两个案例研究，我学到了更多。

sentences.en: But this really can affect people's lives globally, can't it?
sentences.zh: 但这确实会影响人们的全球生活，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think with the Tourette's bit, it's been a condition for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于妥瑞症，它作为一种疾病已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: It has relatively recently changed its name.
sentences.zh: 它的名字在相对近期才有所改变。

sentences.en: So previously in the DSM and the ICD, which is the sort of European and World Health Organization's manual for classifications,
sentences.zh: 之前在DSM和ICD（即欧洲和世界卫生组织的分类手册）中，

sentences.en: it used to be known as the Giles de la Tourette, I think is how you pronounce it.
sentences.zh: 它曾被称为“吉尔斯·德拉·妥瑞”（Giles de la Tourette），我想发音是这样的。

sentences.en: And that's where the Tourette bit comes from.
sentences.zh: 这就是“妥瑞”这个名字的由来。

sentences.en: So they dropped the Giles bit and just stuck with that bit, really.
sentences.zh: 所以他们去掉了“吉尔斯”的部分，只保留了后面那个词。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think it's prevalent across the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为它在世界各地都很普遍。

sentences.en: So lots of people will present with that.
sentences.zh: 很多人都会有这种表现。

sentences.en: But I think the bits that can make it really difficult is because the interventions for it can be quite difficult to put together,
sentences.zh: 但我认为让它变得非常困难的部分在于，针对它的干预措施很难整合，

sentences.en: definitely outside of sort of Western civilization sort of thing, really.
sentences.zh: 特别是在西方文明之外，确实如此。

sentences.en: Often then nothing sort of happens with it.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，对此往往无计可施。

sentences.en: You just get ostracized often because it's uncontrollable, but it's involuntary responses in terms of the vocal tics and the motor tics.
sentences.zh: 你经常会被排斥，因为它无法控制，但就发声抽动和运动抽动而言，它们是不自主的反应。

sentences.en: And because they are involuntary, sometimes they can be causing offense.
sentences.zh: 因为它们是不自主的，有时会引起冒犯。

sentences.en: They can cause difficulties.
sentences.zh: 它们会造成困难。

sentences.en: They can cause a lot of pain for the individual as well, depending on the type of tics that they might have as well.
sentences.zh: 根据患者抽动的类型，它们也可能给个人带来巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: So a lot of physical pain can come about from some of them.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些会导致严重的身体疼痛。

sentences.en: And some can be quite extreme for the person's experience in them as well, really.
sentences.zh: 而且对于患者的亲身经历来说，有些可能相当极端。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there has been a high profile example of that recently, hasn't there?
sentences.zh: 最近有一个高调的例子，不是吗？

sentences.en: With the, I think it was John was the name of the person that was featured in I Swear.
sentences.zh: 就是那个在《我发誓》中出镜的人，名字好像叫约翰。

sentences.en: And he went, I think, was it the BAFTAs or the Golden Globes or the Oscars?
sentences.zh: 他去了，我想是英国电影学院奖（BAFTA）、金球奖还是奥斯卡？

sentences.en: It was some big award ceremony.
sentences.zh: 是某个大型颁奖典礼。

sentences.en: Some big awards, yeah, I'm a bit in the news.
sentences.zh: 某个大型颁奖礼，是的，我在新闻里看到过。

sentences.en: And I think everybody in the audience was warned, you know, we do have the star of the show here today who does have Tourette's.
sentences.zh: 我想当时观众席上的每个人都被提醒了，你知道，我们今天有节目的主角在这里，他患有妥瑞症。

sentences.en: And so if you do hear anything, then please know that that's not someone purposefully causing offense.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你听到什么，请知道那不是有人故意冒犯。

sentences.en: But, of course, Tourette's almost works with kind of the subconscious and kind of preys on the thing that is the least appropriate thing to say sometimes.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，妥瑞症有时几乎是与潜意识协同工作的，它有时会专门针对那些最不合时宜的话题。

sentences.en: And that will come out.
sentences.zh: 然后那些话就会脱口而出。

sentences.en: And I think there was some people of kind of an ethnic, diverse background on the stage.
sentences.zh: 我想当时舞台上有一些来自不同种族背景的人。

sentences.en: And then he said something racist that then everybody heard.
sentences.zh: 然后他说了一些种族主义的话，大家都听到了。

sentences.en: And I think the real Ferrari was not about necessarily the person.
sentences.zh: 我认为真正的愤怒并不一定是因为那个人。

sentences.en: It wasn't about John.
sentences.zh: 不是针对约翰。

sentences.en: It was about the fact that I think it was the BBC were broadcasting on a delay and hadn't chose to then bleep out the expletives in that.
sentences.zh: 而是因为BBC当时是在延迟播出，却没选择消掉其中的脏话。

sentences.en: So that was the bit that really did make the headlines.
sentences.zh: 所以那才是真正登上头条的部分。

sentences.en: And that can be difficult, can't it, for people if they are saying things they don't mean and that they haven't got control of.
sentences.zh: 这确实很困难，不是吗？如果人们说出他们本意并非如此且无法控制的话。

sentences.en: But people will make that kind of cognitive judgment or just a reactive judgment.
sentences.zh: 但人们会做出那种认知判断，或者仅仅是反应性的判断。

sentences.en: Yeah, about what's going on.
sentences.zh: 是的，关于正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And it's, and yeah, I think it was the BBC had not, or whichever broadcaster it was at the time, had not chosen to bleep out, I guess,
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，我想当时BBC，或者当时的任何广播公司，没有选择消音，我想，

sentences.en: that particular bit if they had put it on a delay.
sentences.zh: 如果他们设置了延迟播出，本可以消掉那一部分。

sentences.en: I'm not, I didn't read too much about it at the time because sometimes there's a lot of frior and sometimes it's just easy to let the dust settle and then go back and have a look.
sentences.zh: 我当时没读太多相关报道，因为有时会有很多喧嚣，有时让事情平息后再回头看会更容易。

sentences.en: So I'm not sure how much they were actually putting a delay on.
sentences.zh: 所以我不太确定他们当时到底有没有设置延迟。

sentences.en: I think that was one of the criticisms of the BBC is all, it would have been more helpful.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是对BBC的批评之一，如果能那样做会更有帮助。

sentences.en: But anyway, so yeah, so often with inappropriate language, shall we say in terms of that,
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，是的，所以通常对于不恰当的语言，我们这么说吧，

sentences.en: it's particularly the swearing side of things and saying things that might be offensive or upsetting to other people.
sentences.zh: 特别是说脏话以及说出可能冒犯或让别人难过的话，

sentences.en: It's a relatively tiny proportion of people with Tourette's that actually can struggle with that aspect of how they might express their vocal tics.
sentences.zh: 只有极小比例的妥瑞症患者会真正被这种表达发声抽动的方式所困扰。

sentences.en: But I think because it's the, it's the most shocking and media sensationalized, that's the stuff that people tend to associate Tourette's with in particular, even though, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我认为因为这是最令人震惊且被媒体炒作的部分，所以人们往往倾向于将妥瑞症与此联系起来，尽管你知道，

sentences.en: of 100 people, you know, five to 10 might have some difficulties around expressing in terms of that.
sentences.zh: 100个人里，可能只有5到10个人在表达方面会有一些困难。

sentences.en: But that's the focus it tends to be in terms of that, but it can be a really difficult experience for the person with Tourette's themselves because more often than not,
sentences.zh: 但这往往是关注的焦点，但对于妥瑞症患者本人来说，这可能是一种非常困难的经历，因为通常情况下，

sentences.en: they're just as horrified that they're using that language, but not feeling able to control, not able to stop themselves from expressing that because it doesn't, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们对自己使用这种语言感到同样震惊，但却无法控制，无法阻止自己表达出来，因为它并不，你知道，

sentences.en: I said it's an involuntary sound that comes out.
sentences.zh: 我说过这是一种不自主发出的声音。

sentences.en: Now it's involuntary words, involuntary movement.
sentences.zh: 现在是不自主的词汇，不自主的动作。

sentences.en: So it can make it very difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以这会让情况变得非常困难。

sentences.en: And I think one of the aspects with the film shows is just how isolating that can be, because often you then are aware of how other people react.
sentences.zh: 我认为这部电影展示的其中一个方面就是这有多么孤立，因为你通常会意识到别人的反应。

sentences.en: So you tend not to go into situations, you tend not to put yourself out there, you tend not to interact with others, because the worry about saying or offending something,
sentences.zh: 所以你往往不会去某些场合，往往不会让自己出现在公众视野中，往往不会与他人互动，因为担心说错话、冒犯

sentences.en: somebody or doing something, can make it really difficult.
sentences.zh: 某人或做出什么举动，这会变得非常困难。

sentences.en: And that can feel really,
sentences.zh: 这会让人感到非常、

sentences.en: really lonely if you feel the people around you don't understand or aren't accepting that there are things that are going to happen that are outside of your control.
sentences.zh: 非常孤独，如果你觉得周围的人不理解或不接受那些你无法控制的事情会发生的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's making me think about, I think the first person I'd ever learned of who had this, I think I was maybe studying psychology at the time, I think it was late 90s,
sentences.zh: 是的，这让我想起，我想我第一次听说患有这种病的人，当时我可能正在学习心理学，大概是90年代末，

sentences.en: early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 21世纪初。

sentences.en: It was Pete from Big Brother.
sentences.zh: 是《老大哥》里的皮特。

sentences.en: Does that ring a bell for you?
sentences.zh: 你对他有印象吗？

sentences.en: Oh, we've got it vaguely, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，有点模糊的印象，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Nicky Graham, it was that year, Nicky Graham and Pete.
sentences.zh: 那是尼基·格雷厄姆的那一年，尼基·格雷厄姆和皮特。

sentences.en: And Pete, I think some of Pete's tics would be when he became overstimulated, he'd sort of shout, shout, white goods, white goods.
sentences.zh: 皮特，我想皮特的一些抽动表现是当他过度兴奋时，他会大喊，大喊“白色家电，白色家电”。

sentences.en: And like, that was his thing, like, as in, you know, like your washing machine or your tumble dryer.
sentences.zh: 就像，那是他的口头禅，就像，你知道，比如你的洗衣机或滚筒式烘干机。

sentences.en: So not necessarily going to offend anybody.
sentences.zh: 所以不一定会冒犯任何人。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think sometimes Tourette's gets a kind of reputation as being funny or humorous.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我认为有时妥瑞症会被认为是有趣或幽默的。

sentences.en: And I think that's tricky, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我认为这很棘手，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because you then aren't necessarily seeing the impact this has on your family, on your friends, on your being able to have a relationship,
sentences.zh: 因为你并没有看到这对你的家庭、朋友、你建立人际关系的能力，

sentences.en: on your being able to work and hold down a job.
sentences.zh: 以及你工作和保住工作的能力所产生的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that's definitely been one of the, I suppose, unfortunate media portrayals.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是媒体描绘中不幸的一面。

sentences.en: And for many years,
sentences.zh: 多年来，

sentences.en: there were jokes and a lot of sort of humor around people who might have expressed tics or that somehow it would be funny to have that difficulty in expressing that, really.
sentences.zh: 人们会拿那些可能有抽动表现的人开玩笑，或者觉得有这种表达困难会很滑稽，确实如此。

sentences.en: I, on one hand, I think that's got better to some extent, although I think it is still a really big issue.
sentences.zh: 一方面，我认为这种情况在某种程度上有所好转，尽管我认为这仍然是一个非常大的问题。

sentences.en: And as we can see from what happened with John at the ceremony,
sentences.zh: 正如我们从约翰在颁奖典礼上发生的事情所看到的那样，

sentences.en: there's still quite a lot of misunderstanding and there's still a lot of different difficulties around how do we support people with Tourette's when they're in a situation that is live,
sentences.zh: 仍然存在很多误解，而且在直播情况下，我们该如何支持妥瑞症患者，仍然存在很多困难，

sentences.en: that is going to be broadcast,
sentences.zh: 在即将播出的节目中，

sentences.en: where there is a high likelihood, given it was John's difficulties in particular, that things that might offend or upset other people might be broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 考虑到约翰的具体困难，很有可能会播出冒犯或让别人难过的内容。

sentences.en: And how do we protect both the person with Tourette's and how do we lessen some of the impact that might happen in terms of having that delayed on and then maybe being able to bleep out some bits or cut away or just having a little bit of,
sentences.zh: 我们该如何保护妥瑞症患者，又该如何减轻因延迟播出而可能产生的影响，比如消掉一些片段、切掉画面，或者只是稍微做一点，

sentences.en: okay, what are we going to do if?
sentences.zh: 好的，如果发生了，我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: How are we going to manage?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何应对？

sentences.en: How are we going to support John?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何支持约翰？

sentences.en: Because I suppose that was the bit we didn't hear a lot about is actually he would have been absolutely horrified.
sentences.zh: 因为我想我们没听到太多关于这一点的信息，实际上他当时肯定感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And I think he did release a statement a few days later about how upsetting it is and for him as well to be using language that as an individual he absolutely abhors and wouldn't use,
sentences.zh: 我想他在几天后发表了一份声明，谈到使用他个人绝对厌恶且不会使用的语言是多么令人难过，

sentences.en: but because of the Tourette's and the involuntary nature of what's happening.
sentences.zh: 但因为妥瑞症以及所发生事情的不自主性。

sentences.en: And then having that, not only using that language, but broadcasting it live across the millions of people who are watching it.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅是使用了那种语言，还向数百万观众进行了直播。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm not sure how much support John had then got from others in the BBC after that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不确定在那之后约翰从BBC其他人那里得到了多少支持。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a really good, really good point.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是一个非常、非常好的观点。

sentences.en: Speaking clinically, you know, sometimes I will sit and giggle with clients.
sentences.zh: 从临床角度来说，你知道，有时我会和来访者坐在一起咯咯笑。

sentences.en: And I did when I was in the NHS as well, because so much of it is about having a good relationship and also being a human.
sentences.zh: 我在NHS工作时也这样做过，因为很多时候这关乎建立良好的关系，也关乎作为一个真实的人。

sentences.en: I mean, does stuff crop up that happens with people in your clinic where it is funny?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在你的诊所里，有没有出现过让人觉得好笑的事情？

sentences.en: Or are you always having to kind of suppress that to be very serious and respectful, Jason?
sentences.zh: 还是说，Jason，你总是不得不压抑这种情绪，以保持严肃和尊重？

sentences.en: I'm sorry, that's a really awkward question.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，这个问题问得有点尴尬。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: I think it's a really helpful one.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常有帮助的问题。

sentences.en: And it's, I definitely think in our clinic, so we run a weekly clinic with one of the few NHS trusts that does work with adults, with Tourette's.
sentences.zh: 而且，我绝对认为在我们的诊所——我们每周都会开设诊所，是少数几家为患有妥瑞症的成年人提供服务的国民医疗服务体系（NHS）信托机构之一。

sentences.en: Most services, and there aren't many, to be honest, tend to focus with children, but we work with adults.
sentences.zh: 老实说，大多数服务机构（其实也没几家）往往专注于儿童，但我们是针对成年人的。

sentences.en: And you can have a really, I'm not sure if I'm the right word, but it can be really liberating, I think, often for clients to talk about some of the things they struggle with,
sentences.zh: 你可以进行一次非常——我不确定用这个词是否合适——但我觉得，对来访者来说，谈论他们所挣扎的一些事情，有时真的会让人感到如释重负，

sentences.en: but also some of the situations that have been humorous for them in terms of Tourette's and how that might have manifeSt.
sentences.zh: 同时也包括一些对他们而言与妥瑞症相关的幽默情境，以及这些情况是如何表现出来的。

sentences.en: And yes, there are other elements where it's really uncomfortable and they dislike having them and they cause them a lot of difficulties.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有一些确实让人非常不舒服的方面，他们不喜欢这些症状，这些症状也给他们带来了很多困难。

sentences.en: But there are occasions, I think, where we've interacted with clients and they've been able to talk about the humor side of things when that's happened.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在某些情况下，我们与来访者互动时，当这些事情发生时，他们能够谈论幽默的一面。

sentences.en: There might only be brief moments for them, but there have been occasions, I think, where sometimes expressing those things can be a moment of lightness for them,
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这可能只是短暂的时刻，但我认为确实有过这样的机会，有时表达这些事情对他们来说可能是一种轻松的时刻，

sentences.en: rather than the sort of constant worry and anxiety, particularly when they're outside, what they might feel is their safe space.
sentences.zh: 而不是那种持续的担忧和焦虑，特别是在他们身处室外，即他们认为的“安全空间”之外时。

sentences.en: So often when they're at home, that's usually the time when that sort of happens.
sentences.zh: 所以通常当他们在家里时，那通常是这种情况发生的时候。

sentences.en: It's less likely from what we've seen in our clinics where clients will talk about or experience that outside of being in their safe space or with people who know them really well.
sentences.zh: 根据我们在诊所的观察，来访者在安全空间之外，或者与不太熟悉的人在一起时，谈论或经历这些情况的可能性较小。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢你。

sentences.en: And, you know, just kind of segwaying back to Luke Manton, I really love his work because he, when he was given the diagnosis as an adult,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，回到Luke Manton的话题，我真的很喜欢他的工作，因为当他成年后被诊断出患有妥瑞症时，

sentences.en: was almost sort of told, oh, this is how it's going to be now.
sentences.zh: 他几乎被告知，哦，以后生活就是这样了。

sentences.en: You know, you might as well get familiar with the benefits office because you're likely you'll never work again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你最好还是熟悉一下福利办公室，因为你很可能再也无法工作了。

sentences.en: You know, that's not always the case.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实并非总是如此。

sentences.en: And certainly in his case, he speaks very publicly.
sentences.zh: 当然，就他而言，他非常公开地谈论这些。

sentences.en: So I've never I've never been his psychologiSt. I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有——我从来没有做过他的心理医生。我不是。

sentences.en: I just follow him on social and admire his work.
sentences.zh: 我只是在社交媒体上关注他，并钦佩他的工作。

sentences.en: So he talks very publicly about his experiences and raising awareness of this, but has then built a business which is very successful.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常公开地谈论自己的经历并提高人们的认识，但他随后建立了一家非常成功的企业。

sentences.en: So it is possible, but it obviously it does put barriers, especially with employed work.
sentences.zh: 所以这是可能的，但显然它确实设置了障碍，特别是在就业方面。

sentences.en: It can put barriers in in place for sufferers, can't it, Jason?
sentences.zh: 这确实会给患者带来障碍，不是吗，Jason？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think with depending on who and where you might have got your assessment and what's happening in terms of that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这取决于你在哪里、由谁进行了评估，以及评估过程中发生了什么。

sentences.en: I know that Tourette's Action, which is the national charity for Tourette's in the UK,
sentences.zh: 我知道Tourette's Action，这是英国妥瑞症的国家慈善机构，

sentences.en: does a huge amount of work in terms of both training clinicians who might be interested in doing the diagnostic work,
sentences.zh: 在培训有兴趣进行诊断工作的临床医生方面做了大量工作，

sentences.en: but also in terms of doing some of the intervention work around supporting people with Tourette's to help them develop a measure of control about helping them better understand their Tourette's,
sentences.zh: 同时也进行了一些干预工作，旨在支持妥瑞症患者，帮助他们培养一定的控制力，帮助他们更好地理解自己的妥瑞症，

sentences.en: what's going on and developing strategies for helping lessening some of that impact.
sentences.zh: 了解正在发生什么，并制定策略来帮助减轻其中的一些影响。

sentences.en: Now, unfortunately, we don't have a cure, so we can't stop Tourette's with people.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，目前我们还没有治愈方法，所以我们无法让人们彻底摆脱妥瑞症。

sentences.en: But there is often throughout somebody's lifespan with Tourette's a process of what we call waxing and waning.
sentences.zh: 但在一个人的妥瑞症病程中，通常存在一个我们称之为“起伏”（waxing and waning）的过程。

sentences.en: So sometimes the tics are really prevalent and other times they're not around as much.
sentences.zh: 所以有时抽动症状非常明显，而有时则不那么频繁。

sentences.en: And then something can happen and trigger that.
sentences.zh: 然后可能会发生一些事情并触发它。

sentences.en: So it could be a stress reaction.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一种压力反应。

sentences.en: It could be anxiety, worry.
sentences.zh: 可能是焦虑、担忧。

sentences.en: All these can help increase that bit as well.
sentences.zh: 所有这些也都会加剧这种情况。

sentences.en: And I think when the workplace element to that then can make it really difficult to either find a workplace that's accommodating or understanding enough in terms of that bit really.
sentences.zh: 我认为，当工作场所的因素加入其中时，确实会让人很难找到一个足够包容或理解的工作环境。

sentences.en: But absolutely, Tourette's in and of itself doesn't have to be a barrier to finding work, really.
sentences.zh: 但绝对地，妥瑞症本身并不一定成为寻找工作的障碍，真的。

sentences.en: I think definitely more so with the Equality Act and reasonable adjustments and just even a small amount of understanding
sentences.zh: 我认为在《平等法案》和合理调整的保障下，再加上哪怕一点点的理解，

sentences.en: and just knowing what the myths are around Tourette's and knowing what the reality is,
sentences.zh: 了解关于妥瑞症的误区是什么，了解现实是什么，

sentences.en: I think can help people pursue that life of maybe wanting to work and pursue things they're really interested in.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可以帮助人们追求他们想要的工作生活，并追求他们真正感兴趣的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I'm always very curious about inclusion and having conversations around inclusion.
sentences.zh: 我一直对包容性以及围绕包容性进行的对话非常好奇。

sentences.en: You know, I've had a podcast episode with someone that is registered blind, has a guide dog and is a trainee psychologist,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我曾在一期播客中采访过一位注册盲人，他有导盲犬，还是一位心理学实习生，

sentences.en: you know, someone that uses a wheelchair, someone that's got kind of limb difference.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有使用轮椅的人，有肢体差异的人。

sentences.en: Like, do you or could you imagine a time where we had, you know, a qualified HCPC psychologist with Tourette's?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能想象或者说我们是否能迎来一位患有妥瑞症的合格HCPC心理学家？

sentences.en: Or maybe there was one already and I'm just not aware of them.
sentences.zh: 或者也许已经有一位了，只是我不知道而已。

sentences.en: Yes, it's a short answer.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是：是的。

sentences.en: We could.
sentences.zh: 我们可以。

sentences.en: We may, as I said, we may already have in terms of that.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们可能已经有了。

sentences.en: I think the bits around managing, I suppose, the different presentations of Tourette's that might occur in terms of that.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于管理妥瑞症可能出现的不同表现方面，

sentences.en: I think, yes, anecdotally, I know that we've, as a clinic, we've had other clinicians who've come through and wanting to really get a better understanding
sentences.zh: 我认为，是的，根据经验，我知道我们作为一家诊所，已经有其他临床医生来寻求更好的理解，

sentences.en: and trying to manage how their Tourette's and their tics might present so that they can go on and do clinical work in terms of that bit.
sentences.zh: 并试图管理他们的妥瑞症和抽动症状的表现，以便他们能够继续进行临床工作。

sentences.en: And they were quite keen to try and manage that so that when they were interacting with a client,
sentences.zh: 他们非常渴望尝试管理这一点，以便在与来访者互动时，

sentences.en: they felt that they did have somewhat more of a measure of control about when they might express those tics, really.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己在何时表达这些抽动方面有更多的控制力。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I would not be surprised if we already did have a client psychologist out there who already did have a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，如果已经有一位患有妥瑞症的临床心理学家，我一点也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It might be a case of watch this space.
sentences.zh: 这可能需要拭目以待。

sentences.en: But if that is you, please make yourselves known to us because we would love to be able to see how that is for you.
sentences.zh: 但如果那个人就是你，请让我们知道，因为我们很想了解这对你来说是怎样的体验。

sentences.en: So, you know, not to be too bleak, but you've said there's no cure.
sentences.zh: 那么，不是为了太悲观，但你提到没有治愈方法。

sentences.en: Speaking as a psychologist, is there, I don't know, will formulation help?
sentences.zh: 作为一名心理学家，我想知道，制定个案概念化（formulation）会有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Is there any particular approach or method that can help someone to control this or make a bit of a difference for them?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么特定的方法或手段可以帮助人们控制这种情况，或者为他们带来一些改变？

sentences.en: Yes, is the sure answer.
sentences.zh: 肯定的回答是：有。

sentences.en: So there's two, well, there's several approaches, I think, that can be really helpful.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几种方法可以非常有帮助。

sentences.en: The first one is really understanding what Tourette's is and how it might impact on somebody.
sentences.zh: 第一种是真正理解什么是妥瑞症，以及它可能如何影响一个人。

sentences.en: And I think once people who do have a diagnosis of tics or might have that presentation,
sentences.zh: 我认为一旦那些被诊断出患有抽动症或可能有这种表现的人，

sentences.en: I think when they really begin to understand and get a sense of what that means, both for them and how the sides might are,
sentences.zh: 当他们真正开始理解并意识到这意味着什么，无论是对他们自己还是对周围的人，

sentences.en: I think those are the bits that can be really helpful in terms of empowering them to know what they can do and what they might need some more support with around that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是非常有帮助的，能够赋予他们力量，让他们知道自己能做什么，以及在哪些方面可能需要更多的支持。

sentences.en: And then once they've got the diagnosis being assessed, going into the intervention side of stuff, there's no nice guidelines for Tourette's at the moment.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们得到了诊断并进行了评估，进入干预阶段，目前还没有针对妥瑞症的NICE指南。

sentences.en: So there's no guidelines around what assessment should like.
sentences.zh: 所以没有关于评估应该是什么样子的指南。

sentences.en: There's no guidelines around what intervention should look like.
sentences.zh: 也没有关于干预应该是什么样子的指南。

sentences.en: There are, however, some what they call the nice appraisal stuff.
sentences.zh: 不过，确实有一些所谓的“Nice评估”相关的内容。

sentences.en: So there's some, I think because of AI and the massive advances in technology, their technology appraisal side of nice has been working a little bit faster.
sentences.zh: 我认为由于人工智能和技术的巨大进步，Nice在技术评估方面的工作进展得稍微快了一些。

sentences.en: So there's sometimes they'll agree a technology, but they haven't got a formal guidance.
sentences.zh: 所以有时他们会认可某项技术，但还没有出台正式的指导意见。

sentences.en: So for Tourette's for children, so under 17s, there are some appraisal technologies that say that
sentences.zh: 以儿童（17岁以下）的妥瑞症为例，有一些评估技术指出，

sentences.en: comprehensive behavioural intervention for Tourette's, which is a, I wouldn't say a cognitive behavioural boast one,
sentences.zh: 针对妥瑞症的综合行为干预——我不会称之为认知行为疗法，

sentences.en: but it's a behavioural boast intervention, which usually runs for about eight to 12 sessions.
sentences.zh: 但它是一种行为干预，通常持续8到12次疗程。

sentences.en: There's sort of two main umbrella ones under there.
sentences.zh: 这下面主要涵盖了两种主要的方法。

sentences.en: There's what's known as habit reversal and exposure response in terms of the two main ones, in terms of helping people to understand what's going on, really.
sentences.zh: 即所谓的习惯逆转训练和暴露反应预防，这是帮助人们真正理解自身状况的两种主要手段。

sentences.en: So in terms of the intervention side of stuff, if you are somebody who wants to explore that, there is what's known as a pre-monetary urge.
sentences.zh: 在干预方面，如果你想深入了解，有一种概念叫“前驱冲动”。

sentences.en: So most people or a lot of people with experienced Tourette's have a, I suppose, a sensation that their tics are coming on.
sentences.zh: 大多数或许多妥瑞症患者，我想说，会有种感觉，觉得自己的抽动症要发作了。

sentences.en: And one of the things that both of those interventions looks at is to help people begin to recognise
sentences.zh: 这两种干预措施共同关注的一点是，帮助人们开始识别

sentences.en: and understand when those pre-monetary urges are about to occur and what they then can do to help sit with that
sentences.zh: 并理解这些前驱冲动何时即将发生，以及他们随后可以做些什么来应对这种感觉，

sentences.en: and then help them to lessen the next step, which will often be expressing their tics, really.
sentences.zh: 从而帮助他们减轻下一步的反应，即通常表现出来的抽动行为。

sentences.en: And when we talk with clients in the clinic, we tend to think of it in terms of it's a bit like having an itch and then you scratch the itch.
sentences.zh: 当我们在诊所与客户交流时，我们倾向于将其比作身上发痒，然后你去抓挠那个痒处。

sentences.en: So the itch would be the pre-monetary urge and then the tic would be you scratching it.
sentences.zh: 痒感就是前驱冲动，而抽动就是你去抓挠的动作。

sentences.en: So in the moment, it does seem to feel like it gives you some relief from the urge.
sentences.zh: 所以在那一刻，这似乎确实能让你从冲动中获得一些缓解。

sentences.en: But by doing the tic, you're increasing the likelihood that the next time you have that pre-monetary urge, you're more likely then to act on the tic.
sentences.zh: 但通过做出抽动动作，你实际上增加了下一次出现前驱冲动时，你更倾向于再次做出抽动行为的可能性。

sentences.en: And then what the habit reversal and the ERP is looking at is trying to help people to sit longer with the pre-monetary urge until it fades so that you don't express the tic.
sentences.zh: 习惯逆转训练和暴露反应预防的目的，就是试图帮助人们在面对前驱冲动时坚持更长时间，直到冲动消退，从而避免做出抽动行为。

sentences.en: And there's got sort of two different ways of sort of exploring that with somebody.
sentences.zh: 针对这一点，有大约两种不同的探索方式。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: There's almost some parallel between kind of how we might work with OCD as well then, like trying to tolerate that distress a little bit longer before you take that action.
sentences.zh: 这和我们处理强迫症（OCD）的方式有某种相似之处，都是试图在采取行动之前，多忍受一会儿那种痛苦。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And often there is quite somewhat of an overlap between direct behaviours and possible OCD.
sentences.zh: 直接的行为表现和可能的强迫症之间，往往存在相当程度的重叠。

sentences.en: So often when we work in clinic and we do work, we're trying to separate out what might be tics and what might be an OCD behaviour in terms of some of the things we do really.
sentences.zh: 所以在临床工作中，我们通常会尝试区分哪些可能是抽动，哪些可能是强迫行为。

sentences.en: And I think that sense of helping people to, I suppose, grow their hope that actually just because you might have a diagnosis of Tourette's
sentences.zh: 我认为帮助人们建立希望感很重要，即仅仅因为你被诊断出患有妥瑞症，

sentences.en: doesn't mean that there isn't interventions.
sentences.zh: 并不意味着就没有干预手段了。

sentences.en: There is things that could be really supportive and helpful.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些非常有支持性和帮助性的方法。

sentences.en: I know for our service, we tend to follow the European guidelines around tics and Tourette's
sentences.zh: 我知道在我们的服务中，我们倾向于遵循欧洲关于抽动和妥瑞症的指南，

sentences.en: because there is some European guidelines, there's just no UK ones at the moment, or nice ones in terms of guidance and stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为目前只有欧洲指南，英国暂时还没有相关的Nice指导意见。

sentences.en: And I think it's the first, second and third line of interventions is more behaviourally based.
sentences.zh: 我认为第一、第二和第三线干预措施更多是基于行为的。

sentences.en: There is a little bit where they will talk about it's possible that some medications might be helpful, but it's very much a sort of an off-licence prescription if that happens.
sentences.zh: 虽然有时会提到某些药物可能有效，但这通常属于超说明书用药。

sentences.en: And you would need usually a psychiatrist or a neuropsychiatrist who had a good sense of an understanding of that,
sentences.zh: 而且你通常需要一位对这方面有深刻理解的精神科医生或神经精神科医生，

sentences.en: and they will just trial and error it to help manage some of those behaviours when they're occurring, really.
sentences.zh: 他们会通过反复试验来帮助管理这些行为。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: That's a really helpful overview.
sentences.zh: 这个概述非常有帮助。

sentences.en: And I know people are always thinking about, well, who is more likely to have this?
sentences.zh: 我知道人们总是在想，谁更容易患上这种病？

sentences.en: Is there anything that makes that, you know,
sentences.zh: 有什么因素会导致这种情况吗？

sentences.en: I know when we're looking at something like fibromyalgia or kind of polycystic ovaries, or even kind of things like migraines,
sentences.zh: 我知道当我们观察纤维肌痛、多囊卵巢综合征，甚至是偏头痛这类疾病时，

sentences.en: there's actually evidence that shows us that people with higher kind of adverse childhood scales, scores for adverse events in childhood are more likely to get those conditions.
sentences.zh: 实际上有证据表明，童年时期经历过更多负面事件的人，患这些疾病的可能性更高。

sentences.en: Is that a parallel for Tourette's or is it kind of just random?
sentences.zh: 妥瑞症也是这样吗，还是说这纯属随机？

sentences.en: To some extent, it varies.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，情况各不相同。

sentences.en: There isn't a massive amount of research in Tourette's.
sentences.zh: 关于妥瑞症的研究并不算特别多。

sentences.en: Tourette's action, again, they do quite a lot of work in this area and they fund research into this area as well.
sentences.zh: “妥瑞症行动”（Tourette's Action）组织在这个领域做了大量工作，也资助了相关研究。

sentences.en: There are some elements that are looking at in terms of Tourette's and whether they're particular populations that it might be more occurring in.
sentences.zh: 确实有一些研究在探讨妥瑞症是否在特定人群中更容易发生。

sentences.en: I suppose in terms of that bit where Tourette's and I suppose neurodevelopmental conditions in general really is that you typically seem to see
sentences.zh: 我认为就妥瑞症以及一般的神经发育障碍而言，你通常会发现，

sentences.en: if somebody's likely to present with Tourette's, they're likely to have possibly something else as well.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人表现出妥瑞症，他们很可能同时伴有其他问题。

sentences.en: So that could be a mental health difficulty, so anxiety, mood disorder, possibly OCD.
sentences.zh: 这可能是心理健康问题，比如焦虑、情绪障碍，或者是强迫症。

sentences.en: But they also might present with another neurodevelopmental condition.
sentences.zh: 但他们也可能同时表现出另一种神经发育障碍。

sentences.en: So ADHD is often one that we can sometimes see with autism, which is partly why our service tends to work with all three,
sentences.zh: 比如多动症（ADHD）经常与自闭症同时出现，这也是为什么我们的服务倾向于同时处理这三者，

sentences.en: because there is so much overlap in terms of what we tend to see in terms of the other difficulties that somebody might present with.
sentences.zh: 因为患者表现出的其他困难之间存在很大的重叠。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And there might be a variety of reasons why people are watching or listening to this episode.
sentences.zh: 人们观看或收听这一集的原因可能多种多样。

sentences.en: And one of the options might be that they themselves think they might fulfill a diagnosis or that someone that they care about.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因可能是他们认为自己符合诊断标准，或者他们关心的人符合。

sentences.en: What should someone do if they are experiencing this almost for the first time or they're trying to join up the dots?
sentences.zh: 如果有人几乎是第一次经历这种情况，或者正试图理清头绪，他们应该怎么做？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对的。

sentences.en: Definitely going for a GP because most services will require a GP referral.
sentences.zh: 一定要去看全科医生（GP），因为大多数服务都需要全科医生的转诊。

sentences.en: Depending on where you are in the country, some services may be done via neurology or neuropsychiatry,
sentences.zh: 根据你所在的地区，有些服务可能通过神经科或神经精神科进行，

sentences.en: if you're particularly fortunate to have access to a neuropsychologist in your area.
sentences.zh: 如果你非常幸运，当地有神经心理学家的话。

sentences.en: But GP is generally the first port of call, really.
sentences.zh: 但全科医生通常是第一联系人。

sentences.en: And I definitely think for adults in terms of the diagnosis bit, the bit that it would be useful to think back is, has this always been something I've had?
sentences.zh: 对于成年人来说，在诊断方面，我认为回想一下“这是否一直是我有的问题”很有用。

sentences.en: So did it start in childhood for you?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这是否从童年就开始了？

sentences.en: And it might be that it was present in childhood, but maybe it's gone away.
sentences.zh: 可能它在童年时期就存在，但后来消失了。

sentences.en: So sometimes we've seen clients where they may have had Tourette's tick-like behavior in childhood, but it wasn't formally diagnosed or assessed.
sentences.zh: 我们有时会遇到这样的客户，他们在童年时期可能有过类似妥瑞症的抽动行为，但没有经过正式的诊断或评估。

sentences.en: Well, when I say that, I mean in terms of they might not have done a hour long sort of assessment
sentences.zh: 我指的正式评估是那种长达一小时的问诊，

sentences.en: where they've asked them a range of questions around how often, what's it look like, what parts of your body does it seem to go in, which is what we would typically do.
sentences.zh: 询问关于频率、表现形式、身体哪些部位受影响等一系列问题，这才是我们通常会做的。

sentences.en: But often what we've seen in the notes when people come to us is they might have gone to a healthcare professional,
sentences.zh: 但当人们来到我们这里时，我们经常在病历中看到他们可能曾去看过医疗专业人员，

sentences.en: they've noticed the ticks and they've said they've also got ticks and then that's it.
sentences.zh: 他们提到了抽动，医生也确认了有抽动，然后就没下文了。

sentences.en: There's like a line or a comment and they've moved on.
sentences.zh: 可能就只有一行字或一句评论，然后就跳过了。

sentences.en: Some of that might be, I think, because there's historically always been very difficult to have an intervention for that.
sentences.zh: 我想这部分原因可能是，历史上针对这种情况一直很难进行干预。

sentences.en: So often it was just like we've noticed ticks and then they'll move on to what brought the person through really.
sentences.zh: 所以通常只是记录下“观察到抽动”，然后就转去处理患者当时就诊的主要原因了。

sentences.en: But definitely as an adult, I think if you're thinking about that might explain some of the things
sentences.zh: 但作为成年人，如果你认为这可能解释了你一直以来挣扎的一些问题，

sentences.en: I've struggled with, it's definitely thinking about were these present in childhood?
sentences.zh: 一定要回想一下这些症状在童年时期是否就存在。

sentences.en: If you're not sure, you don't remember, it's worth asking parents.
sentences.zh: 如果你不确定或记不清了，值得去问问父母。

sentences.en: So sometimes people will talk about or parents will comment about, well, they always seem to have hay fever, even though it wasn't hay fever this evening.
sentences.zh: 有时父母会说，他们小时候好像总是有花粉症，尽管那晚并不是花粉症发作。

sentences.en: So they sniffed a lot or they seem to blink a lot or they had a particular twitch or movement.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能只是频繁吸鼻子、频繁眨眼，或者有某种抽动或动作。

sentences.en: And as long as there was a vocal bit alongside that, and then if that's persisted for longer than a year, and then as an adult, if you're experiencing those things,
sentences.zh: 只要伴随有发声症状，且持续时间超过一年，那么作为成年人，如果你正经历这些情况，

sentences.en: then it might be worth having a conversation with the cheap ear.
sentences.zh: 那么或许值得找专业人士聊聊。

sentences.en: I think particularly if it causes a problem for you.
sentences.zh: 我认为特别是当这些症状对你造成困扰时。

sentences.en: For some people, we've had clients who have sort of been referred, but they've said, actually, it's who I am.
sentences.zh: 对于有些人，我们曾接待过一些被转诊来的客户，但他们会说，其实这就是我本来的样子。

sentences.en: Yes, it causes problems and it's difficult, but I can manage it.
sentences.zh: 是的，它确实会造成问题，也很困难，但我可以应对。

sentences.en: And they don't necessarily want to go on and get an assessment and access intervention.
sentences.zh: 他们不一定想要继续进行评估并接受干预。

sentences.en: Whereas other clients have said, actually, this is really, really difficult.
sentences.zh: 而其他客户则会说，实际上，这真的、真的非常困难。

sentences.en: And I absolutely do need some help and support around managing some of this, even if it's to allow other people, healthcare professionals, workplace,
sentences.zh: 我确实需要一些帮助和支持来应对这些情况，哪怕只是为了让其他人、医疗专业人员或工作场所能够理解，

sentences.en: to say, this is why I struggle in these situations.
sentences.zh: 让他们明白这就是我在这些情况下感到挣扎的原因。

sentences.en: These are why my behaviours might come across this way.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我的行为可能会表现出这种方式的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, and obviously, speaking as a qualified psychologist, both of us, we want people to be able to live as full and active life as they would want for themselves, or is feasible.
sentences.zh: 是的，显然，作为两名合格的心理学家，我们都希望人们能够按照他们自己想要的方式，或者在可行的情况下，过上充实而积极的生活。

sentences.en: And as part of that, people might obviously want to get married.
sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，人们显然可能想要结婚。

sentences.en: They might want to have children.
sentences.zh: 他们可能想要孩子。

sentences.en: They might, if they're female, find themselves that they're pregnant, they're expecting.
sentences.zh: 如果她们是女性，可能会发现自己怀孕了，正在期待新生命的到来。

sentences.en: And is that something that will take additional consideration for someone with Tourette's?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于患有妥瑞氏症的人来说，这是否需要额外的考虑呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's not typical, I think, for our service, that we have had concerns around safeguarding in terms of maybe the extent
sentences.zh: 是的，所以对于我们的服务来说，我们对保障方面的担忧并不典型，这可能与某人身上可能发生的妥瑞氏症行为的程度有关。

sentences.en: of the Tourette's behaviour that might be going on for somebody.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，如果可能存在保障问题，我会说这总是如此，那要么是贯穿整个童年的妥瑞氏症，

sentences.en: Often, if there was likely to be a safeguarding in, I'm going to say it's always the case, it would either have been Tourette's that had been present throughout childhood,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们无论如何也不会因为那部分原因来到我们的服务部门。

sentences.en: in which case it wouldn't be coming to our service anyway in terms of that bit.
sentences.zh: 我想我们遇到更多这类情况的是其他可能导致困难的表现。

sentences.en: I suppose the bits where we've had more of that is more other presentations that might have caused difficulties.
sentences.zh: 特别是功能性神经障碍，

sentences.en: So functional neurological disorder in particular,
sentences.zh: 就某人身上可能发生的情况而言，它的表现可能与妥瑞氏症非常相似。

sentences.en: which can present very similar to Tourette's in terms of what might be going on for somebody.
sentences.zh: 然而，让情况变得相当棘手的部分是，这种情况持续多久了？

sentences.en: The bits that make it quite tricky, though, is then how long has this been going on?
sentences.zh: 它是从童年开始的吗？

sentences.en: So did it start in childhood?
sentences.zh: 而通常对于功能性神经障碍来说，它并不是从童年开始的。

sentences.en: Whereas typically for functional neurological disorder, it didn't start in childhood.
sentences.zh: 并不是说它不能，但通常是发生了什么事情。

sentences.en: Not saying it can't, but often something happened.
sentences.zh: 自从那次事件以来，这些行为现在才出现。

sentences.en: And since this event, these behaviours have now been present.
sentences.zh: 另一个困难在于，你也可以同时患有这两种疾病。

sentences.en: And the other difficulty on that is you can also have both.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能同时患有妥瑞氏症、功能性神经障碍以及很多其他疾病，真的。

sentences.en: So you could have Tourette's and functional neurological disorders and tons of things, really.
sentences.zh: 我认为就怀孕方面而言，

sentences.en: I think in terms of the pregnancy side of stuff,
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们诊所里有任何患有妥瑞氏症的孕妇。

sentences.en: I don't think we've had anybody that's come through our clinic who has been pregnant with Tourette's.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有一些客户在运动抽动方面有非常痛苦和困难的经历。

sentences.en: We've had clients who've had some very painful and some very difficult tics in terms of their motor actions.
sentences.zh: 比如自残、剧烈疼痛，几乎就像被锁住了一样，导致身体无法动弹。

sentences.en: Self-hitting themselves, lots of pain, so almost like a lock-in, so they can't move physically.
sentences.zh: 几乎是僵在原地。

sentences.en: It's almost freezing in place.
sentences.zh: 那些确实是非常痛苦的经历。

sentences.en: Those have been quite painful ones, really.
sentences.zh: 所以人们有时确实会遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: So there's an element of that sometimes that occurs for people, really.
sentences.zh: 好的，鉴于这显然是一个相当复杂的诊断过程，而且有时它看起来可能有点像其他疾病，

sentences.en: OK, so given that obviously this can be quite a complicated diagnosis process and that sometimes it might look a bit like something else,
sentences.zh: 在做出妥瑞氏症诊断之前，还有什么你需要纳入或排除的吗，杰森？

sentences.en: is there anything else that you kind of need to rule in or rule out before you go with a Tourette's diagnosis, Jason?
sentences.zh: 是的，有的。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你查看诊断标准时，第四部分的底部内容是，它不能用其他疾病来更好地解释。

sentences.en: So I think when you look at the diagnostic criteria, the bottom part of part four in terms of that is it's not better explained by something else.
sentences.zh: 所以有些身体健康状况看起来像是妥瑞氏症，但可能是其他疾病。

sentences.en: So there are some physical health conditions that look like it could be Tourette's but might be something else.
sentences.zh: 例如，亨廷顿舞蹈症就是其中之一。

sentences.en: So, for example, Huntington's in terms of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们尝试做的是，如果它是作为成人转诊来的，并且是通过全科医生转诊的，有时也来自其他领域，

sentences.en: So what we try to do then is if it comes through as an adult referral and it's come via GP, sometimes it comes other areas,
sentences.zh: 但主要是全科医生，我们可能会要求全科医生先转诊到神经科，以排除任何可能导致这种情况的身体原因。

sentences.en: but primarily it's GPs, we might ask the GP to refer on to neurology first just to rule out any physical cause for what might be going on.
sentences.zh: 同样，如果从转诊单上看，它似乎不是从童年开始的，而是在成年后因某事开始的，

sentences.en: Similarly, if from looking at the referral, it seems to not have had a childhood start but may have started in adulthood after something,
sentences.zh: 那么它可能还包含功能性神经障碍的成分。

sentences.en: it might be there's a functional illogical disorder element to or FND part to it as well.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们可能会要求全科医生转诊到神经科，给他们做一个身体健康检查，以排除，

sentences.en: So that's why we might ask GPs to refer to neurology just to give them a physical health once over really to sort of rule out,
sentences.zh: 好的，我们认为这没有身体基础。

sentences.en: OK, we don't think there's a physical basis for this.
sentences.zh: 然后他们通常会被转回我们这里进行评估。

sentences.en: And then often they then sort of get referred back to us for the assessment side of things potentially.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah, thank you.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会撞击自己的头部之类的，他们有点无法控制。

sentences.en: And sometimes people are hitting their own heads and stuff and they kind of can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这有时会让人们感到害怕。

sentences.en: And I think that can be scary for people at times.
sentences.zh: 关于是否应该尝试约束某人或在这种能力范围内支持他们，有没有一般的经验法则？

sentences.en: And knowing whether you should be trying to restrain someone or support them in that capacity, is there a general rule of thumb?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果有人正在抽动并且有伤害自己的风险，我们应该怎么做，杰森？

sentences.en: Like what ought we to be doing if someone is ticking and at risk of hurting themselves, Jason?
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为对于伤害自己的极端情况，我们倾向于向人们建议的是，

sentences.en: Yeah, I think with the extreme in terms of causing harm to themselves in terms of that bit, where we've tended to suggest to people around that is,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，情况各不相同。

sentences.en: unfortunately, it does vary.
sentences.zh: 对于有些人，如果这更有可能是与妥瑞氏症相关的行为，即正在发生的运动抽动，

sentences.en: For some people, if it is more likely to be behaviour that's linked with Tourette's, so a motor tick that's going on,
sentences.zh: 那么关键在于帮助减少处于可能发生这种情况的环境中的可能性。

sentences.en: it can be about helping to reduce the likelihood of being in a situation where that is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以有时可能是某人正在打自己，或者用东西撞头。

sentences.en: So sometimes it can be where somebody is punching themselves, for example, or hitting their head with something.
sentences.zh: 有时可能在于，好的，我们如何支持那个人？

sentences.en: Sometimes it can be about, okay, how do we support that person?
sentences.zh: 让他们不伤害自己？

sentences.en: Do it to not hurt themselves?
sentences.zh: 是关于穿戴一些保护性的东西，这样他们实际上就不会伤害自己吗？

sentences.en: Is it around wearing something protective so they're actually not hurting themselves?
sentences.zh: 或者我们给他们一些柔软的东西拿着？

sentences.en: Or do we give them something soft to hold?
sentences.zh: 所以可能是在他们打自己时，让他们用那个东西来打，而不是用紧握的手或拳头之类的，真的。

sentences.en: So maybe potentially it's around they're using that to hit themselves rather than a closed hand or a fist or things like that for when hitting themselves, really.
sentences.zh: 但这确实很困难，或者可能非常困难，我认为妥瑞氏症患者中出现这种情况的比例往往要小得多。

sentences.en: But it's a really difficult, or can be a really difficult, I think the proportion of people across Tourette's who have that does tend to be much smaller.
sentences.zh: 通常当达到那种程度或极端时，有时可能确实是，

sentences.en: And often when it's at that level or that extreme, that's sometimes where it might be actually,
sentences.zh: 也许药物治疗可能是他们想要考虑和探索的方向。

sentences.en: maybe medication might be something that they might want to then look at and explore.
sentences.zh: 虽然正如我们所说，并没有真正能帮助控制这种情况的药物。

sentences.en: Although, as we've said, there isn't really a medication to help manage that.
sentences.zh: 但有些药物可以用来帮助人们感到更放松，从而减少他们表现出妥瑞氏症的可能性。

sentences.en: But some of the medications can be used to help make people help them feel more relaxed and therefore they're less likely to express their Tourette's.

sentences.en: that actually did almost stop it in its tracks and made life much more manageable for people.

sentences.en: Obviously, it's a private company, so they say they're the best thing since sliced bread, but if the evidence can back up their claims, then yes, definitely.

sentences.zh: 可以帮助他们显著减少表现出这些抽动行为的时间，

sentences.en: that can help them significantly reduce when they might be expressing those tic behaviour
sentences.zh: 以及他们对自己身上发生的事情的控制力。

sentences.zh: 和不戴手表时，我想他们在两个例子中都在泡茶，你知道，简直是天壤之别。

sentences.en: and not wearing the watch, and I think they were making a cup of tea in both examples, and it was, you know, poles apart.
sentences.zh: 当他们戴着它时，你根本不会知道这个人患有帕金森病，我希望无论这个设备做什么，无论是生物反馈，

sentences.en: When they're wearing the tic, you wouldn't have known that this person had Parkinson's diagnosis, and I would hope that whatever this device does, whether it's biofeedback,
sentences.zh: 还是某种刺激，我希望它真的能对人们有效，这样他们就能从妥瑞氏症的身份中走出来，

sentences.en: because I think it can kind of put a bit of a cloud.
